newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES SIGN GLAVINE TO DEAL WORTH REPORTED $42 MILLION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES SIGN GLAVINE TO DEAL WORTH REPORTED $42 MILLION.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves secured the services of another member of their dominant rotation for the long term, agreeing to a five-year pact with Tom Glavine that reportedly makes the left-hander baseball's highest-paid pitcher.

Glavine agreed to a four-year deal with a club option for a fifth season. The ESPN cable network reported the package to be worth $42 million over the five seasons including a $4 million signing bonus.
"To say I'm happy would probably be an understatement," Glavine said at a news conference Thursday.
"I wanted to be part of this organisation. I wanted to stay here and now that's a reality. I want to keep pitching well and help this team win and win some more world championships."
The annual average of Glavine's reported deal is $8.4 million, exceeding the contracts given to Braves teammate John Smoltz and Roger Clemens of the Toronto Blue Jays.
Clemens, a three-time American League Cy Young Award winner, left the Boston Red Sox and signed a three-year, $24.75 million deal with Toronto, an average of $8.25 million.
Smoltz, who won the 1996 National League Cy Young Award, was re-signed last October for $31 million over four years, an average of $7.75 million per season.

"Excellent pitching has been the cornerstone of our success the last six years," said general manager John Schuerholz, whose team has competed in four of the last five World Series, winning the championship over Cleveland in 1995.
"Tom has been one of those cornerstones and we're delighted to know that he will continue as a member of the Braves organisation."
Glavine, 31, has 121 wins in the 1990s, more than any pitcher except teammate Greg Maddux (125). Glavine is in the final year of a five-year deal that pays him $5 million this season.

Glavine won the 1991 Cy Young and was runner-up to Maddux in 1992. He finished third in the voting the next three years. He is 5-2 with a 2.08 ERA this year and has a career mark of 144-94 with a 3.41 ERA.
"I guess for the moment I am the highest-paid pitcher. But I'm sure next year when my contract kicks in, Mr. Maddux and somebody else will get more," Glavine said.

The contract leaves Maddux as the only key member of the Braves who is not signed to a long-term deal. Maddux, who has won a record four Cy Young Awards, can become a free agent at the end of the season but is expected to be re-signed.
